title: The Annunciation
text: The angel Gabriel brings Mary God's message, and Mary says yes. — Fra Angelico, c. 1440–1445

title: The Annunciation
text: Young Mary listens as God's light fills her room. — Henry Ossawa Tanner, 1898

title: The Visitation
text: Mary hurries to visit her cousin Elizabeth, and they share their joy. — Domenico Ghirlandaio, 1491

title: Adoration of the Shepherds
text: The shepherds come to see baby Jesus, and his light shines on every face. — Gerard van Honthorst, 1622

title: The Nativity
text: Mary lays baby Jesus in the manger while angels sing above. — Giotto, c. 1305

title: Adoration of the Magi
text: Kings from far away follow the star and kneel before the child Jesus. — Gentile da Fabriano, 1423

title: The Presentation in the Temple
text: Mary and Joseph bring baby Jesus to God's house, and old Simeon holds him. — Giotto, c. 1305

title: The Flight into Egypt
text: Joseph keeps Mary and baby Jesus safe on the long road to Egypt. — Giotto, c. 1305

title: Jesus among the Doctors
text: Twelve-year-old Jesus listens and asks questions in the Temple. — Albrecht Dürer, 1506

title: The Baptism of Christ
text: John baptizes Jesus, and the Holy Spirit comes down like a dove. — Andrea del Verrocchio and Leonardo da Vinci, c. 1470–1475

title: The Wedding at Cana
text: At a big wedding feast, Jesus does his first miracle: water becomes wine. — Paolo Veronese, 1563

title: The Calling of Saint Matthew
text: Jesus points to Matthew at his money table and says, "Follow me." — Caravaggio, 1599–1600

title: The Sermon on the Mount
text: Jesus teaches the crowd on a hillside how to be truly happy. — Carl Bloch, 1877

title: Christ Blessing the Children
text: Mothers bring their little ones, and Jesus welcomes and blesses them. — Lucas Cranach the Elder, after 1537

title: The Good Shepherd
text: Jesus carries a lost lamb home, and the flock follows him. — Bernhard Plockhorst, 19th century

title: The Return of the Prodigal Son
text: The father hugs his son who came home — God always welcomes us back. — Rembrandt, c. 1668

title: Christ in the Storm on the Sea of Galilee
text: The waves are huge, but Jesus is in the boat with his friends. — Rembrandt, 1633

title: Walking on the Water
text: Jesus walks on the sea and tells his friends not to be afraid. — Ivan Aivazovsky, 1888

title: The Entry into Jerusalem
text: People wave branches and lay down cloaks as Jesus rides into the city. — Giotto, c. 1305

title: The Last Supper
text: At his last meal, Jesus gives his friends the gift of the Eucharist. — Leonardo da Vinci, 1495–1498

title: Christ in Gethsemane
text: Jesus prays in the garden and trusts his Father. — Heinrich Hofmann, 1886

title: Christ Carrying the Cross
text: Jesus carries his cross with love for us. — El Greco, c. 1590–1595

title: Christ Crucified
text: Jesus gives his life on the cross because he loves us so much. — Diego Velázquez, c. 1632

title: Noli me tangere
text: On Easter morning in the garden, the risen Jesus calls Mary Magdalene by name. — Fra Angelico, c. 1440–1442

title: The Supper at Emmaus
text: Two disciples recognize the risen Jesus when he breaks the bread. — Caravaggio, 1601

title: The Ascension
text: Jesus goes up to heaven and promises to send the Holy Spirit. — John Singleton Copley, 1775

title: Pentecost
text: The Holy Spirit comes like tongues of fire on Mary and the apostles. — El Greco, c. 1600

set: Mary and the Holy Family in Art
title: The Assumption of the Virgin
text: Mary is taken up, body and soul, into the glory of heaven. — Titian, 1516–1518

set: Mary and the Holy Family in Art
title: The Coronation of the Virgin
text: Jesus crowns his mother Mary as Queen of heaven, with saints and angels all around. — Fra Angelico, c. 1430–1432

set: Mary and the Holy Family in Art
title: The Immaculate Conception
text: God kept Mary free from sin from the very first moment of her life. — Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, c. 1678

set: Mary and the Holy Family in Art
title: The Sistine Madonna
text: Mary brings baby Jesus to us — and two little angels watch from below. — Raphael, c. 1512–1513

set: Mary and the Holy Family in Art
title: Madonna of the Goldfinch
text: Little John the Baptist shows Jesus a goldfinch while Mary reads. — Raphael, c. 1505–1506

set: Mary and the Holy Family in Art
title: The Holy Family with a Little Bird
text: At home in Nazareth, Jesus plays with a little dog and a bird while Mary and Joseph work. — Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, c. 1650

set: Mary and the Holy Family in Art
title: Saint Joseph the Carpenter
text: Young Jesus holds a candle while Joseph works with wood. — Georges de La Tour, c. 1642

set: Mary and the Holy Family in Art
title: The Heavenly and Earthly Trinities
text: Jesus stands between Mary and Joseph, with God the Father and the Holy Spirit above. — Bartolomé Esteban Murillo, c. 1675–1682

set: Mary and the Holy Family in Art
title: The Angelus
text: Two farmers stop work to pray when the church bell rings. — Jean-François Millet, 1857–1859

set: Bible Stories and Saints in Art
title: Noah's Ark
text: Two by two, the animals walk into the ark before the flood. — Edward Hicks, 1846

set: Bible Stories and Saints in Art
title: The Peaceable Kingdom
text: A painting of Isaiah's promise: wild and tame animals together in peace. — Edward Hicks, c. 1834

set: Bible Stories and Saints in Art
title: Moses with the Ten Commandments
text: Moses holds up the stone tablets of God's law. — Rembrandt, 1659

set: Bible Stories and Saints in Art
title: Daniel's Answer to the King
text: Daniel trusts God, and the lions do not hurt him. — Briton Rivière, 1890

set: Bible Stories and Saints in Art
title: The Conversion of Saint Paul
text: On the road to Damascus, a bright light from Jesus changes Saul's life. — Caravaggio, c. 1600–1601

set: Bible Stories and Saints in Art
title: Saint Francis Preaching to the Birds
text: St. Francis tells the birds to praise God, their Creator. — Giotto (attributed), c. 1297–1299

title: The Light of the World
text: Jesus knocks at the door of our heart — the door opens from the inside. — William Holman Hunt, 1851–1856 (this version)

title: The Guardian Angel
text: A guardian angel watches over two children crossing a dangerous path. — Bernhard Plockhorst, 19th century

title: Christ Pantocrator
text: One of the oldest icons of Jesus: he blesses us and holds the Gospel. — Unknown iconographer, 6th century

title: Our Lady of Guadalupe
text: The image of Mary on St. Juan Diego's tilma, honored by millions of pilgrims. — Image on St. Juan Diego's tilma, 1531

title: Our Lady of Perpetual Help
text: Baby Jesus holds his mother's hand tightly — Mary always helps us. — Unknown Cretan iconographer, 15th century

title: The Sign of the Cross
text: In the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

title: The Our Father (The Lord's Prayer)
text: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name; thy kingdom come, thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us; and lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. Amen.

title: The Hail Mary
text: Hail, Mary, full of grace, the Lord is with thee. Blessed art thou among women and blessed is the fruit of thy womb, Jesus. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us sinners, now and at the hour of our death. Amen.

title: The Glory Be
text: Glory be to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, as it was in the beginning is now, and ever shall be world without end. Amen.

title: The Apostles' Creed
text: I believe in God, the Father almighty, Creator of heaven and earth, and in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, who was conceived by the Holy Spirit, born of the Virgin Mary, suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, died and was buried; he descended into hell; on the third day he rose again from the dead; he ascended into heaven, and is seated at the right hand of God the Father almighty; from there he will come to judge the living and the dead. I believe in the Holy Spirit, the holy catholic Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and life everlasting. Amen.

title: Act of Contrition
text: O my God, I am heartily sorry for having offended you, and I detest all my sins because of your just punishments, but most of all because they offend you, my God, who are all good and deserving of all my love. I firmly resolve, with the help of your grace, to sin no more and to avoid the near occasions of sin. Amen.

title: Guardian Angel Prayer
text: Angel of God, my guardian dear, to whom God's love commits me here, ever this day be at my side, to light and guard, to rule and guide. Amen.

title: Grace Before Meals
text: Bless us, O Lord, and these thy gifts, which we are about to receive from thy bounty, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

title: Grace After Meals
text: We give thee thanks, for all thy benefits, Almighty God, who live and reign for ever. [And may the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.] Amen.

title: Glory to God (Gloria) – Angels' Song
text: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace to people of good will.

title: Morning Offering
text: O Jesus, through the Immaculate Heart of Mary, I offer you my prayers, works, joys and sufferings of this day for all the intentions of your Sacred Heart, in union with the Holy Sacrifice of the Mass throughout the world, for the salvation of souls, the reparation for sins, the reunion of all Christians, and in particular for the intentions of the Holy Father this month. Amen.

title: Angel of the Lord (The Angelus)
text: V. The Angel of the Lord declared unto Mary. R. And she conceived of the Holy Spirit. Hail Mary... V. Behold the handmaid of the Lord. R. Be it done unto me according to thy word. Hail Mary... V. And the Word was made flesh. R. And dwelt among us. Hail Mary... V. Pray for us, O holy Mother of God. R. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ. Let us pray: Pour forth, we beseech thee, O Lord, thy grace into our hearts; that we, to whom the Incarnation of Christ, thy Son, was made known by the message of an angel, may by his Passion and Cross be brought to the glory of his Resurrection. Through the same Christ our Lord. Amen.

title: The Memorare
text: Remember, O most gracious Virgin Mary, that never was it known that anyone who fled to thy protection, implored thy help, or sought thine intercession was left unaided. Inspired by this confidence, I fly unto thee, O Virgin of virgins, my Mother; to thee do I come, before thee I stand, sinful and sorrowful. O Mother of the Word Incarnate, despise not my petitions, but in thy mercy hear and answer me. Amen.

title: Hail, Holy Queen (Salve Regina)
text: Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope. To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve; to thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this valley of tears. Turn then, most gracious advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us; and after this our exile, show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus. O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

title: Queen of Heaven (Regina Caeli)
text: Queen of heaven, rejoice, alleluia. The Son whom you merited to bear, alleluia, has risen as he said, alleluia. Pray for us to God, alleluia.

title: Come, Holy Spirit
text: V. Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful. R. And kindle in them the fire of your love. V. Send forth your Spirit and they shall be created. R. And you shall renew the face of the earth.

title: Eternal Rest
text: Eternal rest grant unto them, O Lord, and let perpetual light shine upon them. May the souls of all the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace. Amen.

title: Saint Michael Prayer
text: St. Michael the Archangel, defend us in battle, be our protection against the wickedness and snares of the Devil. May God rebuke him, we humbly pray. And do thou, O Prince of the Heavenly Host, by the Power of God, thrust into hell Satan and all evil spirits who wander the earth seeking the ruin of souls. Amen.

title: Act of Faith
text: O my God, I firmly believe that you are one God in three divine Persons, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. I believe that your divine Son became man and died for our sins and that he will come to judge the living and the dead. I believe these and all the truths which the Holy Catholic Church teaches because you have revealed them who are eternal truth and wisdom, who can neither deceive nor be deceived. In this faith I intend to live and die. Amen.

title: Act of Hope
text: O Lord God, I hope by your grace for the pardon of all my sins and after life here to gain eternal happiness because you have promised it who are infinitely powerful, faithful, kind, and merciful. In this hope I intend to live and die. Amen.

title: Act of Love
text: O Lord God, I love you above all things and I love my neighbor for your sake because you are the highest, infinite and perfect good, worthy of all my love. In this love I intend to live and die. Amen.

title: Soul of Christ (Anima Christi)
text: Soul of Christ, be my sanctification. Body of Christ, be my salvation. Blood of Christ, fill all my veins. Water of Christ's side, wash out my stains. Passion of Christ, my comfort be. O good Jesu, listen to me. In Thy wounds I fain would hide, Ne'er to be parted from Thy side, Guard me, should the foe assail me. Call me when my life shall fail me. Bid me come to Thee above, With Thy saints to sing Thy love, World without end. Amen.

title: Spiritual Communion
text: My Jesus, I believe that you are present in the Most Blessed Sacrament. I love you above all things, and I desire to receive you into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive you sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace you as if you were already there and unite myself wholly to you. Never permit me to be separated from you. Amen.

title: The Divine Praises
text: Blessed be God. Blessed be his holy Name. Blessed be Jesus Christ, true God and true Man. Blessed be the name of Jesus. Blessed be his most Sacred Heart. Blessed be his most Precious Blood. Blessed be Jesus in the most holy Sacrament of the altar. Blessed be the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete. Blessed be the great Mother of God, Mary most holy. Blessed be her holy and Immaculate Conception. Blessed be her glorious Assumption. Blessed be the name of Mary, Virgin and Mother. Blessed be Saint Joseph, her most chaste spouse. Blessed be God in his angels and in his saints.

title: We Fly to Thy Patronage (Sub Tuum)
text: We fly to thy patronage, O holy Mother of God; despise not our petitions in our necessities, but deliver us always from all dangers, O glorious and blessed Virgin. Amen.

title: My Soul Magnifies the Lord (Magnificat)
text: My soul proclaims the greatness of the Lord; my spirit rejoices in God my savior.

title: Night Song of Simeon (Nunc Dimittis)
text: Now, Master, you may let your servant go in peace, according to your word.

title: The Lord Is My Shepherd
Christ Be With Me (St. Patrick's Breastplate)
text: Christ with me, Christ before me, Christ behind me, Christ in me, Christ beneath me, Christ above me, Christ on my right, Christ on my left.

title: The Jesus Prayer
text: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of the living God, have mercy on me, a sinner.

title: Jesus, I Trust in You
text: Jesus, I trust in you.

title: O My Jesus (Fatima Prayer)
text: O my Jesus, forgive us our sins, save us from the fires of hell, lead all souls to Heaven, especially those who have most need of your mercy.

title: How to Pray the Rosary
text: Pray the Rosary: think about Jesus' life with Mary.

title: Joyful 1: The Annunciation
text: The Angel Gabriel tells Mary she will be the Mother of Jesus.

title: Joyful 2: The Visitation
text: Mary visits her cousin Elizabeth.

title: Joyful 3: The Nativity
text: Jesus is born in Bethlehem.

title: Joyful 4: The Presentation
text: Mary and Joseph present Jesus in the Temple.

title: Joyful 5: The Finding in the Temple
text: Mary and Joseph find Jesus in the Temple.

title: Luminous 1: The Baptism of Jesus
text: Jesus is baptized in the Jordan.

title: Luminous 2: The Wedding at Cana
text: Jesus turns water into wine.

title: Luminous 3: The Proclamation of the Kingdom
text: Jesus tells everyone about God's Kingdom.

title: Luminous 4: The Transfiguration
text: Jesus shines with God's glory.

title: Luminous 5: The Institution of the Eucharist
text: Jesus gives us his Body and Blood.

title: Sorrowful 1: The Agony in the Garden
text: Jesus prays in the garden.

title: Sorrowful 2: The Scourging at the Pillar
text: Jesus suffers for us.

title: Sorrowful 3: The Crowning with Thorns
text: Jesus is crowned with thorns.

title: Sorrowful 4: The Carrying of the Cross
text: Jesus carries his cross.

title: Sorrowful 5: The Crucifixion
text: Jesus dies on the cross for love of us.

title: Glorious 1: The Resurrection
text: Jesus rises from the dead!

title: Glorious 2: The Ascension
text: Jesus goes up to heaven.

title: Glorious 3: The Descent of the Holy Spirit
text: The Holy Spirit comes at Pentecost.

title: Glorious 4: The Assumption of Mary
text: Mary is taken up to heaven.

title: Glorious 5: The Coronation of Mary
text: Mary is crowned Queen of Heaven and Earth.

title: My Morning Prayer
text: Good morning, God! Thank you for this new day. Help me to be kind and to love like Jesus. Amen.

title: My Night Prayer
text: Thank you, God, for today. I'm sorry for anything I did wrong. Keep my family safe tonight. Good night, Jesus! Amen.

title: Prayer Before School
text: Jesus, be with me at school today. Help me to learn, to listen, and to be a good friend. Amen.

title: Prayer for My Family
text: Dear Jesus, bless my family. Help us to love each other like the Holy Family. Amen.

title: Prayer When I'm Scared
text: Jesus, I am a little scared. Hold my hand and stay with me. I trust in you. Amen.

title: Prayer When I'm Sad
text: Jesus, you know how I feel. Please give me your peace and a big hug. Amen.

title: Thank-You Prayer
text: Thank you, God, for the sun, the trees, my friends and my family! Amen.

title: Prayer for Someone Who Is Sick
text: Dear Jesus, please help ___ to get better. Hold them close to your heart. Amen.

title: Prayer for God's Creation
text: God, you made the whole world! Help me take care of it. Amen.

title: Birthday Blessing
text: Happy birthday! God made you wonderful and loves you so much. Amen.

title: Sorry Prayer (for little ones)
text: Jesus, I'm sorry. I want to do better. Help me to love you and others. Amen.

title: Prayer Before Reading the Bible
text: Holy Spirit, open my heart to hear God's Word. Amen.

title: Five-Finger Prayer
text: Thumb: people close to me. Pointer: teachers. Middle: leaders. Ring: the sick. Pinky: me!

title: The Seven Sacraments
text: Seven special signs where Jesus gives us his grace.

title: Baptism
text: Baptism makes us children of God and washes away sin.

title: Confirmation
text: Confirmation fills us with the gifts of the Holy Spirit.

title: The Holy Eucharist
text: Jesus gives us himself — his Body and Blood.

title: Reconciliation (Confession)
text: Jesus forgives our sins and gives us peace.

title: Anointing of the Sick
text: Jesus comforts and strengthens people who are sick.

title: Holy Orders
text: Some men are called to serve as deacons, priests, and bishops.

title: Matrimony
text: What God has joined together, no human being must separate.

title: Signs of Baptism
text: Water, oil, a white garment, and a candle.

title: Godparents
text: Godparents help you grow in faith.

title: Your Baptism Day
text: Celebrate your baptism birthday!

title: The Holy Oils
text: Three holy oils: chrism, catechumens, and the sick.

title: Choosing a Confirmation Saint
text: Pick a saint to be your special friend in heaven.

title: My First Holy Communion
text: Jesus comes to me in Holy Communion!

title: How to Receive Holy Communion
text: Bow, receive Jesus reverently, and say "Amen."

title: The Eucharistic Fast
text: We fast for one hour before Holy Communion.

title: Real Presence
text: The bread and wine become Jesus' Body and Blood.

title: Eucharistic Adoration
text: Spend time with Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament.

title: Steps of Confession
text: 1. Think. 2. Tell. 3. Be sorry. 4. Do your penance.

title: Examination of Conscience
text: How did I love God and others today?

title: Sacramentals
text: Holy things that help us pray.

title: Blessings
text: God blesses us through his Church.

title: Holy Water
text: Holy water reminds us of our Baptism.

title: The Domestic Church
text: Your family is a little church!

title: Saint Peter
text: Jesus gave Peter the keys of the Kingdom.

title: Saint Andrew
text: Andrew brought his brother Peter to Jesus.

title: Saint James the Greater
text: James was one of Jesus' closest friends.

title: Saint John the Apostle
text: "As I have loved you, so you also should love one another."

title: Saint Philip
text: "Master, show us the Father."

title: Saint Bartholomew (Nathanael)
text: Jesus saw Nathanael under the fig tree.

title: Saint Thomas
text: "My Lord and my God!"

title: Saint Matthew
text: Matthew left his money table to follow Jesus.

title: Saint James the Less
text: James was a faithful leader of the Church in Jerusalem.

title: Saint Jude (Thaddeus)
text: St. Jude, patron of hope.

title: Saint Simon
text: Simon gave his whole heart to Jesus.

title: Saint Matthias
text: Matthias was chosen to take Judas' place.

title: Saint Paul
text: Paul traveled the world to tell everyone about Jesus.

title: Saint Mark
text: Mark wrote the Gospel that begins with John the Baptist.

title: Saint Luke
text: Luke wrote about Jesus' birth and the shepherds.

title: Saint Joseph the Worker
text: St. Joseph worked hard with love.

title: Saints Joachim and Anne
text: Grandparents of Jesus!

title: Saint Mary Magdalene
text: Mary Magdalene was the first to see the risen Jesus.

title: Saints Martha, Mary and Lazarus
text: Jesus' friends in Bethany.

title: Saint Stephen
text: The first martyr forgave those who hurt him.

title: Saint Kateri Tekakwitha
text: The Lily of the Mohawks loved Jesus and prayed in the woods.

title: Saint Elizabeth Ann Seton
text: The first American-born saint.

title: Saint John Neumann
text: A bishop who built many Catholic schools.

title: Saint André Bessette
text: A humble doorkeeper who loved St. Joseph.

title: Saint Marguerite Bourgeoys
text: She opened the first school in Montreal.

title: Saint Marie of the Incarnation
text: A brave Ursuline sister who taught in Quebec.

title: Saint François de Laval
text: The first bishop of Quebec.

title: Saint Marguerite d'Youville
text: The first Canadian-born saint cared for the poor.

title: Canadian / North American Martyrs
text: Brave missionaries who gave their lives to share Jesus.

title: Saint Katharine Drexel
text: She gave her fortune to build schools for Native American and Black children.

title: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini
text: The patron saint of immigrants.

title: Saint Rose Philippine Duchesne
text: "The woman who prays always."

title: Saint Junípero Serra
text: He walked many miles to tell people about Jesus.

title: Saint Damien of Molokai
text: He cared for the sick that others were afraid of.

title: Saint Marianne Cope
text: A kind nurse sister in Hawaii.

title: Saint Juan Diego
text: Mary sent Juan Diego roses in winter, and her image appeared on his tilma.

title: Saint Peter Claver
text: He served enslaved people with love.

title: Saint Isidore the Farmer
text: A farmer who prayed while he worked.

title: Saint Augustine
text: "Our heart is restless until it rests in you."

title: Saint Monica
text: She prayed for her son for many years.

title: Saint Thomas Aquinas
text: A big thinker who loved Jesus in the Eucharist.

title: Saint Jerome
text: He translated the Bible into Latin.

title: Saint Gregory the Great
text: A pope who loved music and helped the poor.

title: Saint Ambrose
text: A bishop with words as sweet as honey.

title: Saint Teresa of Ávila
text: "Let nothing disturb you."

title: Saint John of the Cross
text: He wrote poems about God's love.

title: Saint Catherine of Siena
text: A brave young woman who gave advice to popes.

title: Saint Thérèse of Lisieux (The Little Flower)
text: The Little Way: do little things with great love.

title: Saint Francis de Sales
text: Be who you are, and be that well.

title: Saint Hildegard of Bingen
text: She loved music, plants, and the light of God.

title: Saint Francis of Assisi
text: He loved God and all of God's creatures.

title: Saint Clare of Assisi
text: She shone with the light of Jesus.

title: Saint Benedict
text: Pray and work!

title: Saint Scholastica
text: Benedict's twin sister loved to pray.

title: Saint Dominic
text: He preached and shared the Rosary.

title: Saint Ignatius of Loyola
text: Do everything for the greater glory of God.

title: Saint Francis Xavier
text: He sailed to Asia to tell people about Jesus.

title: Saint Vincent de Paul
text: He helped the poor and the sick.

title: Saint John Bosco
text: He played games with boys to bring them to Jesus.

title: Saint Philip Neri
text: The saint of joy and laughter!

title: Saint Teresa of Calcutta
text: Do small things with great love.

title: Saint Martin de Porres
text: He cared for everyone — even the mice!

title: Saint Rose of Lima
text: The first saint of the Americas.

title: Saint Martin of Tours
text: He shared his cloak with a poor man.

title: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary
text: A princess who fed the hungry.

title: Saint Josephine Bakhita
text: She found freedom and joy in God's love.

title: Saint John Vianney
text: A kind priest who heard confessions every day.

title: Saint Padre Pio
text: "Pray, hope, and don't worry."

title: Saint Maximilian Kolbe
text: He gave his life to save another.

title: Saint Faustina Kowalska
text: Jesus is full of mercy.

title: Saint Gianna Beretta Molla
text: A loving doctor, wife and mother.

title: Saints Louis and Zélie Martin
text: A holy mother and father.

title: Saint Agnes
text: A brave girl who belonged to Jesus.

title: Saint Lucy
text: Her name means light!

title: Saint George
text: A brave knight who trusted God.

title: Saint Joan of Arc
text: A brave girl who followed God's call.

title: Saints Perpetua and Felicity
text: Two brave young mothers who stayed faithful together.

title: Saint Paul Miki and Companions
text: Japanese martyrs who forgave with joy.

title: Saint Charles Lwanga and Companions
text: The brave Uganda Martyrs.

title: Saint Andrew Dung-Lac and Companions
text: Vietnamese martyrs who loved Jesus.

title: Saint Lorenzo Ruiz
text: The first Filipino saint.

title: Saint Lawrence
text: He said the poor are the treasures of the Church.

title: Saint Thomas More
text: "The king's good servant, but God's first."

title: Saint Maria Goretti
text: A brave girl who forgave.

title: Saint Patrick
text: He taught Ireland about the Trinity with a shamrock.

title: Saint Brigid of Kildare
text: A kind abbess of Ireland.

title: Saint David of Wales
text: "Do the little things."

title: Saint Columba
text: He brought the Gospel to Scotland.

title: Saint Mary MacKillop
text: Australia's first saint loved poor children.

title: Saint Alphonsa
text: India's first woman saint.

title: Saint Tarcisius
text: A boy who carried Jesus in the Eucharist.

title: Saint Pancras
text: A brave boy saint of Rome.

title: Saint Kizito
text: The youngest Uganda Martyr.

title: Saint Dominic Savio
text: A joyful boy who wanted to become a saint.

title: Saints Francisco and Jacinta Marto
text: Two young shepherds who saw Our Lady at Fatima.

title: Saint José Sánchez del Río
text: A brave Mexican boy who loved Christ the King.

title: Saint Carlo Acutis
text: A teenager who loved the Eucharist and computers.

title: Saint Pier Giorgio Frassati
text: "Verso l'alto" — to the heights!

title: Saint Bernadette Soubirous
text: Mary spoke to Bernadette at Lourdes.

title: Saint Nicholas
text: A kind bishop who gave secret gifts.

title: Saint Anthony of Padua
text: St. Anthony, please help us find what is lost!

title: Saint Blaise
text: St. Blaise, protect our throats!

title: Saint Cecilia
text: She sang to God in her heart.

title: Saint Christopher
text: Christ-bearer, protect travelers.

title: Saint Rita of Cascia
text: The saint of impossible causes.

title: Saint John Paul II
text: "Be not afraid!"

title: Saint Boniface
text: He told people about Jesus in Germany.

title: Saint Cyril and Saint Methodius
text: Brothers who made an alphabet to share the Bible.

title: Saint Michael the Archangel
text: Who is like God?

title: Saint Gabriel the Archangel
text: God's messenger of good news.

title: Saint Raphael the Archangel
text: God heals!

title: Saints Andrew Kim Taegon, Paul Chong Hasang and Companions
text: Korea's brave martyrs: a young priest, a teacher, and many families who loved Jesus.

title: Saint Anthony the Abbot

text: China's martyrs who stayed faithful to Jesus.

title: The First Commandment
text: I am the LORD your God: you shall not have strange Gods before me.

title: The Second Commandment
text: You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain.

title: The Third Commandment
text: Remember to keep holy the LORD'S Day.

title: The Fourth Commandment
text: Honor your father and your mother.

title: The Fifth Commandment
text: You shall not kill.

title: The Sixth Commandment
text: You shall not commit adultery.

title: The Seventh Commandment
text: You shall not steal.

title: The Eighth Commandment
text: You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.

title: The Ninth Commandment
text: You shall not covet your neighbor's wife.

title: The Tenth Commandment
text: You shall not covet your neighbor's goods.

title: The Great Commandment
text: You shall love the Lord, your God, with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. … You shall love your neighbor as yourself.

title: Blessed Are the Poor in Spirit
text: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

title: Blessed Are They Who Mourn
text: Blessed are they who mourn, for they will be comforted.

title: Blessed Are the Meek
text: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the land.

title: Blessed Are They Who Hunger and Thirst for Righteousness
text: Blessed are they who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be satisfied.

title: Blessed Are the Merciful
text: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.

title: Blessed Are the Clean of Heart
text: Blessed are the clean of heart, for they will see God.

title: Blessed Are the Peacemakers
text: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

title: Blessed Are They Who Are Persecuted for the Sake of Righteousness
text: Blessed are they who are persecuted for the sake of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

title: Feed the Hungry
text: Feed the hungry.

title: Give Drink to the Thirsty
text: Give drink to the thirsty.

title: Clothe the Naked
text: Clothe the naked.

title: Shelter the Homeless
text: Shelter the homeless.

title: Visit the Sick
text: Visit the sick.

title: Visit the Imprisoned
text: Visit the imprisoned.

title: Bury the Dead
text: Bury the dead.

title: Instruct the Ignorant
text: Teach others about God.

title: Counsel the Doubtful
text: Help people who are unsure.

title: Admonish the Sinner
text: Kindly help others choose what is right.

title: Bear Wrongs Patiently
text: Be patient when others are unkind.

title: Forgive Offenses Willingly
text: Forgive others.

title: Comfort the Afflicted
text: Comfort people who are sad.

title: Pray for the Living and the Dead
text: Pray for everyone, living and dead.

title: Wisdom
text: Wisdom: seeing things the way God sees them.

title: Understanding
text: Understanding: knowing God's truth in your heart.

title: Counsel (Right Judgment)
text: Counsel: choosing what is right.

title: Fortitude (Courage)
text: Fortitude: being brave for God.

title: Knowledge
text: Knowledge: knowing God through his creation.

title: Piety (Reverence)
text: Piety: loving God like a child loves a parent.

title: Fear of the Lord (Wonder and Awe)
text: Wonder and awe at how great God is.

title: The Twelve Fruits of the Spirit
text: Charity, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, generosity, gentleness, faithfulness, modesty, self-control, chastity.

title: Faith
text: Faith: believing in God and all he has told us.

title: Hope
text: Hope: trusting God's promises.

title: Charity (Love)
text: Faith, hope, love remain, these three; but the greatest of these is love.

title: Prudence
text: Prudence: thinking before you act.

title: Justice
text: Justice: giving everyone what is fair.

title: Fortitude
text: Fortitude: being strong when it's hard.

title: Temperance
text: Temperance: enough is enough.

title: Go to Mass on Sundays and Holy Days
text: Attend Mass on Sundays and holy days of obligation.

title: Go to Confession at Least Once a Year
text: Confess your sins at least once a year.

title: Receive Holy Communion during Easter Time
text: Receive Holy Communion at least during the Easter season.

title: Keep the Days of Fasting and Abstinence
text: Fast and abstain on the days the Church asks.

title: Help the Church
text: Help provide for the needs of the Church.
